title: Call Center and Cashier session responsibilities and operation guards
scope: Compare active CallCenter WinUI and Cashier WinUI session state, permissions, unresolved-operation guards and delivery checkout shift admission. This is a bounded role-specific comparison, not a global session audit.
decision: The common permission predicate and per-user view-model caching serve parallel session roles. Call Center intentionally discovers the single global open shift before delivery checkout because it does not own a drawer/shift; Cashier retains an operator-selected shift and additionally tracks pending management commands. Call Center HasUnresolvedOperation relies on CanEditOperation, which includes IsOperationBusy; Cashier redundantly checks IsOperationBusy as well, so no current busy-state divergence is shown. No new finding.

behavior.shared: Both process-local sessions hold CurrentUser and shift identity, check permission with all-or-specific, and cache one workflow VM per logged-in user.
behavior.callCenter: RefreshCurrentShiftAsync queries the server global current shift, clears local shift fields on failure, and checkout rechecks before building request; this reflects station has no drawer/owned shift.
behavior.cashier: HasUnresolvedOperation includes management operation owners and cached cashier VM pending/busy states; cashier workflow uses own opened/selected shift and handles broader till operations.
behavior.equivalence: Call Center !CanEditOperation and Cashier !CanEditOperation || IsOperationBusy have same busy implication for the inspected CashierViewModel.State getter, where CanEditOperation already includes !IsOperationBusy.

counterevidence_and_limits: Different station responsibilities make shift and pending-command policies intentionally non-identical. Server CheckoutOrderHandler independently checks the submitted shift is Open; the client refresh/request has a possible time-of-check/time-of-use interval but that is covered by the existing checkout/shift-close analysis and is not newly asserted here. Does not review legacy WPF cashier app, all login/session code, or every header/lock caller.
recommendation: Keep role-specific shift ownership and pending-command semantics explicit. If factoring shared permission/session helpers, do not collapse Call Center global-shift discovery into cashier-owned shift lifecycle. Add focused tests only if session lifecycle is refactored; include no-open-shift, shift-closes-between-refresh-and-checkout, unresolved checkout, and pending cashier management action cases.
required_tests: Call Center checkout stops and clears local shift when GET current shift fails.
Call Center refreshes global shift immediately before new checkout and uses the returned ID.
Cashier blocks lock/close while IsOperationBusy or pending financial command.
If common session logic is introduced, verify all/specific permission behavior in both clients.
related_findings: Existing checkout/shift-close semantic comparison; no new finding.
limitations: Source comparison only; no UI/runtime tests and no database/network activity.
